tools.name: pve_list_endpoints
tools.description: List Proxmox VE API endpoints (operationId, method, path, category, description, read/write, destructive). Filter by category, resource, method, reads/writes, or search. Use this to discover an endpoint, then pve_describe_endpoint for its parameters and pve_call_endpoint to execute it.

category.description: Filter by category (call with no args to see all categories).

resource.description: Filter by resource = the path's first segment, e.g. 'nodes', 'cluster', 'access'.

method.description: Filter by HTTP method: GET, POST, PUT, or DELETE.

search.description: Case-insensitive substring match on operationId, path, name, or description.

limit.description: Max endpoints to return (default 200). Narrow with filters/search for big surfaces.

tools.name: pve_describe_endpoint
tools.description: Get the full spec for one Proxmox VE endpoint: method, path, path params, query/body params (with types, formats, enums, constraints), the response schema, required permissions, and a request sample. Call before pve_call_endpoint so you send exactly the right params.

operation_id.description: The endpoint operationId, e.g. 'get_nodes' or 'post_nodes_node_qemu'. See list_endpoints.

tools.name: pve_call_endpoint
tools.description: Call a Proxmox VE API endpoint and return its JSON response. Validates the operationId and required path params against the catalog, enforces the read-only write gate, then executes. Reads (GET) always run; writes (POST/PUT/DELETE) run only when enabled via PROXMOX_ALLOW_WRITES=true (all surfaces) or PVE_ALLOW_WRITES=true (this surface only). Use pve_describe_endpoint first to learn the exact params.

operation_id.description: The endpoint operationId to call, e.g. 'get_nodes'. See list_endpoints / describe_endpoint.

path_params.description: Values for {placeholder} path params, e.g. { node: 'pve1', vmid: 100 }.

params.description: Non-path params: query params for GET/DELETE, JSON body fields for POST/PUT. See describe_endpoint.

confirm.description: Must be true to execute a DESTRUCTIVE operation (delete/stop/reset/migrate/etc.), even when writes are enabled.
